title: Surprise! Situational Awareness was the bottom
summary_bullets: AI-focused hedge fund Situational Awareness collapsed in July, losing $35 billion
Strong corporate earnings (86% of U.S. companies beat expectations) helped the market recover
Chip stocks rebounded +17% from recent lows as investors refocused on profits rather than AI trade risks
Major indexes reached fresh all-time highs following earnings surprises
full_text:
Stocks have taken a beating recently as investors dump one-time darlings of the AI trade, but they will rebound, according to Fundstrat Global Advisors cofounder Tom Lee, who has a [strong recent track record of market forecasts](https://fortune.com/2025/03/09/stock-market-outlook-sp500-rebound-selloff-trump-tariffs-fed-put/).

Recommended Video

* * *

Chip stocks in particular have been leading the decline, which left the S&P 500 down 1.6% for the week and the Nasdaq off 2.9%. The latest catalyst was the [release of a Chinese AI model](https://fortune.com/2026/07/17/china-moonshot-kimi-k3-markets-china-ai/) that cast doubt on hyperscalers’ gargantuan spending plans.

In an [interview on CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/07/17/market-pullback-is-healthy-says-fundstrats-tom-lee.html) on Friday, Lee argued that the companies selling off are at the center of “one of the most important strategic initiatives” for the U.S., namely AI, and they still have years of runway ahead.

The market pullback is actually healthy because it reduces speculation ahead of upcoming earnings reports from the AI sector, he added.

“I would still stick with those,” Lee said. “I think those names are going to bounce later this year. So I don’t think that the trade is over.”

But he acknowledged that the ubiquity of leverage in the market today is fueling more volatility, calling zero-day trading options and leveraged funds “push-button liquidity for everybody.”

In fact, margin debt is up 54% annually, marking the sixth biggest surge in the last 60 years, Lee estimated. After the other five top increases, the market similarly consolidated.

That dynamic was evident in South Korea, which has experienced a nationwide stock-trading mania as chipmakers [SK](https://fortune.com/company/sk-holdings/) Hynix and [Samsung](https://fortune.com/company/samsung-electronics/) ride the AI wave.

Frenzied demand for more ways to capture upside from those stocks gave rise to leveraged ETFs that further stoked the country’s market rally.

But the Korean stock boom has gone bust in recent weeks. The once-soaring Kospi index has plunged 27% after a hitting a record high last month, putting it well into bear market territory.

As a result, 1.2 million brokerage accounts had a margin call, representing as much as 10% of Korea’s accounts, according to Lee. As traders are forced to sell holdings to cover margin debt, a massive correction followed.

That’s sending ripples across global markets, which have been especially sensitive to moves to bellwether stocks in the AI trade.

For example, SK Hynix’s comments last month that it planned to slow down its AI memory business sparked the Kospi’s fifth worst daily plunge and dragged down indexes around the world.

But compared to the Kospi 27% crash, the S&P 500’s 2% dip from its recent high and the Nasdaq’s 6% slide look like speed bumps. And Lee sees that as a positive sign.

“That’s why a rolling correction that we’re seeing now is super healthy because it’s not the whole market coming down,” he explained. “It’s just pockets of it, and people have ballast like owning the Mag 7 or the software stocks.” 

Still, bond investors, who are less swayed by market fads than stock investors are, have also lost enthusiasm for the AI boom.

As hyperscalers spend hundreds of billions of dollars a year to build data centers and other infrastructure, they are increasingly issuing debt.

But bond investors are showing signs that [demand is waning](https://fortune.com/2026/07/17/ai-boom-debt-blitz-investor-demand-hyperscaler-bond-issuance/). Torsten Slok, chief economists at Apollo Global, pointed out in a note on Wednesday [hyperscalers’ cover ratio](https://www.apollo.com/insights-news/insights/daily-spark/cover-ratios-for-hyperscaler-bonds-declining?utm_medium=email&utm_source=pardot&utm_id=82a16a5a97bdc38f2f053868570c523e&utm_campaign=701Dp00000017sOIAQ&utm_content=body-image-dailyspark-chart1)—investor orders per every dollar of bonds—has plunged.

It was nearly 5x in February 2026 but tumbled to below 2x in July, “suggesting investors may need wider spreads to absorb additional hyperscaler supply,” he warned. By contrast, the ratio for investment grade bonds overall only slipped by about half a point in that span.

The dollar bond market, the world’s largest, has become so saturated that tech giants have been issuing debt in other currencies. As a result, issuers will likely have to provide more attractive terms, meaning their borrowing costs will rise.

AI-related debt must also compete against the flood of debt coming from the Treasury Department as the federal deficit continues to deepen and is on track to hit $2 trillion this fiscal year.

“The current hyperscaler widening is a byproduct of the high-grade investor community trying to rationally price in an accelerating pace of issuance,” JPMorgan strategists wrote in a note on Tuesday.

Shopify Inc.’s [SHOP-T](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/SHOP-T/ "https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/SHOP-T/") share price jumped 16 per cent Wednesday after the company reported strong second-quarter revenue and profit growth that beat analysts’ estimates, driven by the development of [AI](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/topics/artificial-intelligence/ "https://www.theglobeandmail.com/topics/artificial-intelligence/") tools that are attracting more merchants to use its services.

The Ottawa-based e-commerce giant has seen growth from agentic commerce, which is the use of autonomous AI agents to search for and buy products online. Shopify has been building AI tools to help make it easier for shoppers to find online retailers, pushing up the total value of goods sold on its platform.

“We have a very strong conviction that commerce experiences will soon be built in to everywhere people are spending their time,” Shopify president Harley Finkelstein told analysts during a call to discuss the quarterly earnings.

The stronger-than-expected results likely alleviated some investor fears around growing competition for Shopify, after the company’s stock price underperformed in recent months, Citi analyst Tyler Radke wrote in a research note.

“The results appear to be driven by balanced growth across North America and Europe, and we suspect accelerated share gains among larger merchants,” he said.

Shopify’s shares closed at $201.97 Wednesday on the Toronto Stock Exchange.

The company, which reports in U.S. dollars, said its second-quarter revenue rose to US$3.6-billion, up nearly 34 per cent compared with the same period last year. That exceeded analysts’ expectations of US$3.4-billion, according to average estimates compiled by S&P Capital IQ.

Net income climbed to US$1.5-billion, or US$1.16 a share, up from US$906-million or 70 US cents a share in the same period in 2025.

More merchants are now making use of Shopify’s AI tools – such as its Sidekick assistant, which can help with store set-up and design, and later, provide analytics.

However, greater use of these tools had been increasing the company’s AI costs, Shopify noted in its previous earnings call, in May.

More recently, the company has been rebalancing its innovation with greater cost control, executives said on Wednesday’s call.

“The way we think about these models is, we use the best model for the job. We use frontier intelligence where it matters; we use less-expensive models where it’s simply not needed,” Mr. Finkelstein said.

Shopify has also partnered with companies such as OpenAI, Google and Microsoft Corp. to offer its products through user conversations with chatbots or searches, boosting its merchants’ sales.

[With AI costs rising, companies are hiring experts to answer a crucial question: Is it worth it?](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/article-ai-costs-rising-companies-hiring-experts-is-it-worth-it/)

The company reported a 32-per-cent increase in gross merchandise volume, which is the value of transactions made over Shopify’s platform.

Catalog, one AI tool the company has built, enhances merchants’ product data to provide more specific information when consumers are searching for things to buy, Mr. Finkelstein said.

He gave the example of looking for a screenless phone for his 10-year-old daughter.

“Five years ago, I would have done that in \[online\] search, and I probably would have received some big-box retailer selling a bunch of different random products,” he said.

Instead, he was directed to a product called Tin Can, which is a landline-style phone that uses WiFi to make calls, and is specifically designed to introduce children to talking on the phone. The company is also a client of Shopify’s.

Shopify’s “magic sauce,” Mr. Finkelstein added, is offering a variety of products that merchants can use depending on their needs – from small e-commerce sites just beginning to build their presence, to much larger and more complex businesses that require in-depth analytics tools.

“We want to make sure that anyone who’s starting a business at their mom’s kitchen table uses Shopify. We know not all will succeed,” he said, “but what we’ve seen over 20 years, \[is that\] the ones that do, stay with us indefinitely.”

title: Gen Z's $8 pastry habit

# The Gen Z reality check

Despite low savings, Gen Z continue to prioritize experiences and “little treats,” with gig work supporting spending for some.

![Headshot of Taylor Bowley](/content/dam/bank-of-america-institute/contributor-headshots/Taylor-Bowley-Headshot.png)

Taylor Bowley

![Headshot of Lynelle Huskey](/content/dam/bank-of-america-institute/contributor-headshots/Lynelle-Huskey-Headshot.jpg)

Lynelle Huskey

August 2026

## Key takeaways

*   Gen Z have the lowest savings-to-spending ratio of any generation, yet spending growth has remained resilient. They have been the exception to the "K-shaped" pattern, as all income cohorts within Gen Z have exhibited strong spending growth over the past six months, according to Bank of America credit and debit card data.
*   Gen Z discretionary spending has strengthened across beauty, jewelry, coffee and travel, according to Bank of America payments data. This suggests younger consumers are prioritizing purchases and experiences that deliver immediate gratification - consistent with the "little treat economy".
*   To maintain these spending priorities and pursue longer-term goals, Gen Z may be seeking additional income sources. A tougher labor market for new entrants - with many not getting the hours or income they would like - has coincided with increasing gig work. Bank of America account data found nearly 40% of Gen Z gig work comes from social commerce platforms.
*   In this publication, we separate Gen Z fact from fiction, examining popular narratives about the generation through the lens of Bank of America data to better understand their spending behaviors, financial priorities and economic influence.

Read our [full analysis](/content/dam/economic-insights/gen-z-reality-check.pdf) for a more in-depth look at these trends.

Disney

The Walt [Disney](https://deadline.com/tag/disney/) Company and [TikTok](https://deadline.com/tag/tiktok/) today announced a global deal that will allow social media content creators and fans to access and use memorable scenes from Disney movies and shows. 

The new pact, which will pilot in the US in the coming months with other markets to follow, will bring a collection of curated Disney-centric fan-created content from TikTok to the Disney+ app. At launch, short-form videos from participating creators who opt-in to the program will live on both TikTok and Disney+ verticals. The shorts will feature characters and stories from Disney’s brands including Pixar, Marvel, Star Wars, FX and more.

# BMW is putting Spider-Man ads on your dashboard, after promising it never would

## In another attempt to monetize cars after purchase, BMW is framing this as a "one-time movie partnership"

_By [Skye Jacobs](https://www.techspot.com/community/staff/skye-jacobs.149167/) August 3, 2026, 10:47 [29 comments](#commentsOffset) [Add TechSpot](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=https://www.techspot.com "Add TechSpot as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google")_

 [![BMW is putting Spider-Man ads on your dashboard, after promising it never would](https://www.techspot.com/images2/news/bigimage/2026/08/2026-08-03-image-8.jpg)](https://www.techspot.com/images2/news/bigimage/2026/08/2026-08-03-image-8.jpg)

Serving tech enthusiasts for over 25 years.  
TechSpot means tech analysis and advice [you can trust](https://www.techspot.com/ethics.html).

**Sounding off:** BMW is putting a Spider-Man animation on the center screens of compatible cars as part of a movie promotion, drawing criticism because the campaign clashes with the company's earlier claim that the display is a private space. The campaign effectively turns a car's main screen into a branded advertising surface, which is precisely the kind of use BMW previously said it would not pursue.

The [promotion](https://www.theautopian.com/bmw-is-showing-commercials-on-their-cars-dash-screens-and-they-want-you-to-think-its-a-treat/) began on July 27, 2026, and is scheduled to run through August 10 across more than 70 markets. On supported vehicles, starting the car brings up a banner on the Control Display, and tapping it launches a full-screen Spider-Man animation with music and ambient lighting effects. BMW says the feature is available on suitably equipped cars built after July 2020 and running BMW Operating System 7, 8, 8.5, 9, or X.

The ad is being [pitched as](https://www.press.bmwgroup.com/global/article/detail/T0459622EN/bmw-brings-modern-mobility-to-the-sony-pictures-film-%E2%80%9Cspider-man%E2%84%A2:-brand-new-day%E2%80%9D) a tie-in to Spider-Man: Brand New Day, rather than a permanent change to the car. BMW told The Autopian that the in-car animation is part of a broader brand partnership with the film. The company also noted that some BMW vehicles appear in the movie and that a special iX3 was shown at the Los Angeles premiere.

> – Sheel Mohnot (@pitdesi) [August 3, 2026](https://x.com/pitdesi/status/2084418458062872764?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

The reaction has been sharp because the ad appears inside a product customers have already bought. BMW is not selling a streaming subscription or offering a free app here; it is placing commercial content on the dashboard screen that drivers use every time they start the vehicle. That is where the private-space argument comes in: the car's cabin is supposed to feel personal, not like a billboard.

BMW's past comments make the backlash easier to understand. In December 2023, Stephan Durach, BMW Group's senior vice president for connected company development, [said](https://www.bmwblog.com/2023/12/15/bmw-no-ads-inside-cars/) during an industry roundtable, "To say I'm selling the screen to play a commercial. I don't see it. It's a private space."

The company's earlier heated-seat [subscription](https://www.edmunds.com/car-news/bmw-relents-on-heated-seat-subscription.html) still hangs over the issue. BMW charged drivers to activate heated seats that were already installed in their cars, then dropped the subscription in 2023 following criticism. That episode was part of a broader trend around "functions on demand," in which hardware already installed in a vehicle is monetized later through software and recurring fees.

[![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%2016%209'%3E%3C/svg%3E)](https://www.techspot.com/images2/news/bigimage/2026/08/2026-08-03-image-9.jpg)

The Spider-Man campaign is not the same as charging for heated seats, but it fits into the same broader strategy: using software, connected services, and the in-car interface to create revenue after the sale. The difference is that, this time, the product being sold is attention rather than access to a physical feature.

BMW has not said that it has changed its position on in-car advertising, at least not publicly. What is clear is that the company has framed this as a limited film partnership rather than a broader advertising policy, which may explain how the campaign went from idea to rollout. That still leaves the basic tension in place: a branded message is now appearing where BMW once said no commercial should appear.

#### // Related Stories

*   [HallPass says its embarrassing AI-generated candy typos were intentional rage bait](https://www.techspot.com/news/113470-hallpass-embarrassing-ai-generated-candy-typos-actually-intentional.html)
*   [BMW brings color changing tech closer to production with the iX3 Flow Edition](https://www.techspot.com/news/112186-bmw-brings-color-changing-tech-closer-production-ix3.html)

One reason this type of promotion may be becoming more common is that connected cars give automakers a direct path to the driver's screen. Another is that partnerships with movie studios can be packaged as marketing collaborations rather than advertisements, even when the result looks and feels like an ad to the driver.

In this case, the evidence points to a one-off campaign tied to a film launch, but it also shows how software-defined vehicles are turning the dashboard into a place where automakers can monetize drivers' attention in new ways.

# Gene-edited beagles may offer a future option for people with dog allergies

Scientists at a biotech company have used gene editing to switch off a gene that produces the main allergy-causing protein in dogs. It’s the first time this technique has been successful in dogs. Findings were published in the CRISPR Journal. (AP Video/Mary Conlon)

# Hudson Williams Has Made The Most Unexpected Item Completely Sell Out In Canada, And The Internet Couldn’t Be More Surprised

I must admit...I WANT ONE!

Posted on Aug. 5, 2026

## For anyone who's not Canadian, something you should know is that we're weirdly proud of a few things: [_Heated Rivalry_](https://www.buzzfeed.com/jennifer_mcphee/heated-rivalry-sexiest-show-to-watch-reactions) (duh), [Ryan Gosling](https://www.buzzfeed.com/noradominick/spring-movie-preview-2026), [Joni Mitchell](https://www.buzzfeed.com/jennifer_mcphee/joni-mitchell-wins-juno-lifetime-achievement-award), Purdys chocolate, and…[Canadian Tire](https://www.canadiantire.ca/en/pdp/canadian-tire-branded-plaid-reusable-bag-11x14-5x10-4-in-2425514p.html).

## If you've never heard of it, Canadian Tire is our ultimate hardware store...that also fixes cars. You can buy patio furniture, pick up lumber for your next DIY Pinterest inspiration, get windshield-wiping fluid...all while a mechanic changes your tires. It's basically Home Depot with a garage and Canadian flags.

  ![Canadian Tire store exterior with large signage visible](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2026-08/05/14/subbuzz/tTC9FEehY.jpg?downsize=700%3A%2A&output-quality=auto&output-format=auto)

NicolasMcComber / Getty Images

## And Canadian [_Heated_](https://www.buzzfeed.com/jennifer_mcphee/heated-rivalry-ilya-or-shane-personality-quiz) [_Rivalry_](https://www.buzzfeed.com/jennifer_mcphee/heated-rivalry-ilya-or-shane-personality-quiz) star [Hudson William](https://www.buzzfeed.com/jennifer_mcphee/heated-rivalry-lead-actors-connor-storrie-hudson-williams) only had to walk around with an item from Canadian Tire for one afternoon with his costar, [Connor Storrie](https://www.buzzfeed.com/noradominick/heated-rivalry-character-quiz), to make it HOT. And the item will COMPLETELY shock you. It wasn't a hockey stick, a power drill, or a pair of hiking boots — it was a reusable shopping bag. More specifically, a red plaid Canadian Tire tote bag.

  ![Reusable shopping bag with a plaid pattern and a "Canadian Tire" logo on the side](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2026-08/05/13/subbuzz/96mk5mC_R.png?downsize=700%3A%2A&output-quality=auto&output-format=auto)

Canadian Tire

## [According to CBC](https://www.cbc.ca/news/entertainment/hudson-williams-canadian-tire-tote-9.7295988), Canadian Tire employees have already started calling it the "[Hudson Williams bag](https://x.com/deuxmoiworld/status/2083632947647631653/photo/1)." And if you're thinking you can just pop into a store and grab one for yourself, think again. Because according to CBC, _every_ store across the Greater Toronto Area has completely sold out.

![Person on the red carpet wearing a tailored suit with a silky shirt, smiling at the event for the Academy of Canadian Cinema &amp; Television](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2026-08/05/14/subbuzz/APLgb3sXP.jpg?crop=489:404;84,33)

Mathew Tsang / WireImage

Check out the pics of Hudson Williams with the bag _[here](https://x.com/deuxmoiworld/status/2083632947647631653/photo/1)._  

## Turns out, it wasn't even _remotely_ popular before the paparazzi photos of Connor and Hudson. A Canadian Tire employee told CBC, "I was very shocked when I heard, 'Oh, that one got trendy.'" The employee went on to say that the bag had been a "slow mover" in sales, and the store had been trying to clear its inventory because hardly anyone was buying it. Enter...Hudson Williams.

![Three people standing in an aisle of a store, two wearing aprons and one holding a microphone, appearing to conduct an interview](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2026-08/05/14/subbuzz/GvOrBv1kE.png)

## And once the photo started making the rounds online, some Canadians were quick to take advantage of the opportunity. One Canadian Tire employee told CBC, "There was a guy actually who first came in, and he said some famous guy had a bag or something, and how it's going to sell out quick. So he came and bought five bags." Honestly, that was a pretty smart move. As a Toronto girl, I kind of wish I could get my hands on one of those totes now.

# Hackers steal over $130M by exploiting bug in offline hardware wallets

[Lorenzo Franceschi-Bicchierai](https://techcrunch.com/author/lorenzo-franceschi-bicchierai/)

9:27 AM PDT · August 4, 2026

[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Ftechcrunch.com%2F2026%2F08%2F04%2Fhackers-steal-over-130-million-by-exploiting-bug-in-offline-hardware-wallets%2F)[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftechcrunch.com%2F2026%2F08%2F04%2Fhackers-steal-over-130-million-by-exploiting-bug-in-offline-hardware-wallets%2F&text=Hackers+steal+over+%24130M+by+exploiting+bug+in+offline+hardware+wallets&via=techcrunch)[](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftechcrunch.com%2F2026%2F08%2F04%2Fhackers-steal-over-130-million-by-exploiting-bug-in-offline-hardware-wallets%2F&title=Hackers+steal+over+%24130M+by+exploiting+bug+in+offline+hardware+wallets&summary=A+security+vulnerability+in+the+cryptocurrency+hardware+wallet+Coldcard+is+allowing+hackers+to+drain+the+crypto+from+victims%E2%80%99+wallets.+The+total+losses+amount+to+more+than+%24130+million%2C+according+to+blockchain-monitoring+firms.&mini=1&source=TechCrunch)[](https://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftechcrunch.com%2F2026%2F08%2F04%2Fhackers-steal-over-130-million-by-exploiting-bug-in-offline-hardware-wallets%2F&title=Hackers+steal+over+%24130M+by+exploiting+bug+in+offline+hardware+wallets)[](mailto:?subject=Hackers+steal+over+%24130M+by+exploiting+bug+in+offline+hardware+wallets&body=Article%3A+https%3A%2F%2Ftechcrunch.com%2F2026%2F08%2F04%2Fhackers-steal-over-130-million-by-exploiting-bug-in-offline-hardware-wallets%2F)[](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/04/hackers-steal-over-130-million-by-exploiting-bug-in-offline-hardware-wallets/)

Hackers are in the midst of a massive theft of cryptocurrency from supposedly secure offline hardware wallets, according to blockchain security firms monitoring the heists.

At least a dozen different hackers are said to be targeting Bitcoin owners who use the hardware crypto wallet Coldcard, made by Coinkite. At this point, it’s unclear who is behind the digital robberies, and it appears like there’s more than one group of hackers, [according to Galaxy Research](https://x.com/glxyresearch/status/2084411904924045370/photo/1). 

As of Tuesday, the research firm said the hackers have stolen around $130 million. Tom Robinson, the co-founder and chief scientist of crypto-monitoring firm Elliptic, told TechCrunch that the estimate is roughly correct. 

This is the latest effort to steal large amounts of people’s cryptocurrency. So far this year, [according to blockchain-monitoring firm TRM Labs](https://www.trmlabs.com/resources/blog/h1-2026-crypto-hacks-reach-record-high-as-losses-fall-below-usd-1-billion), there have been more than 200 hacks targeting cryptocurrency companies, with a total loss of more than $950 million. 

What makes the ongoing hacks against Coldcard wallet owners particularly interesting is that the point of using a product like Coldcard is that it’s supposed to be, at least in theory, one of the safer ways to store their cryptocurrency. 

Bitcoin owners can store the secret key or seed phrase — essentially a password — to their cryptocurrency in a Coldcard wallet, a device that is not connected to the internet. With this system, Bitcoins are still on the blockchain, like all Bitcoins, but are protected by a password that lives exclusively offline. This is considered a “cold” wallet, as opposed to “hot” wallets that are online, such as those in apps, browser extensions, and accounts on commercial crypto exchanges like Binance or Coinbase. 

As it turns out, hackers figured out that there was a flaw in how Coldcard wallets generated users’ seed phrases, which were predictable, [according to security researchers at Block](https://engineering.block.xyz/blog/predictable-rng-fallback-and-32-bit-reseed-in-coldcard-firmware). Once they figured out the flaw, hackers simply needed to brute-force and generate the victims’ seed phrases. 

By knowing how to make the keys, the hackers did not need to break into the safe that holds them. The hackers essentially figured out how to cut keys at scale.

“Perhaps the hardest part about this is that I did everything right,” Jonathan Goodman, who claimed to have had $1.6 million stolen from his Coldcard wallet, [wrote on X](https://x.com/itscoachgoodman/status/2083527082223563157). “I never shared my seed phrase with anybody. My devices never touched the internet. Everything was kept in multiple safes and safety deposit boxes,” he said. 

“None of it mattered. All because the hardware that created the seed phrase originally had one line in their code from 2021 that had a vulnerability,” wrote Goodman.

In an advisory published on Thursday and updated on Saturday, [Coinkite alerted users of the flaw](https://blog.coinkite.com/coldcard-mk3-seed-generation-warning/), urged them to update their devices, and then “migrate” to a new seed phrase. 

Coinkite did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment.
